title: Vayera: Abimelech (Genesis 20)
hookLine: a foreign king turns out more upright than Abraham feared

cards: You move to a new town, or start a new job, or travel somewhere far away. Before you've met anyone, you've already decided a few things. People here are cold.
People here can't be trusted. Better keep your guard up. Sometimes that instinct protects you.

And sometimes it's just wrong, and the people you braced against turn out to be decent. Abraham, the great hero of this portion, the one who just argued for strangers, walks into a foreign town with exactly that fear.

teach.b: Abraham and Sarah travel to Gerar, ruled by a king named Abimelech. Abraham tells people Sarah is his sister, not his wife. So Abimelech, thinking she's unmarried, takes her into his house.
That night God comes to Abimelech in a dream and warns him: she's a married woman. Abimelech, who hasn't touched her, protests. He asks God, in effect, will you destroy even a righteous nation?
He said she was his sister. She said he was her brother.

teach.h: A CLEAN HEART AND CLEAN HANDS.
teach.b: I did this with a clean heart and clean hands. Listen to that question. It echoes Abraham's own from yesterday, shall not the Judge of all the earth do justly, now in the mouth of a foreign king.
And God agrees: I know you did this with a clean heart; that's why I kept you from sinning. Return her. The text adds something: Abraham is a prophet, and he'll pray for you.
In the morning Abimelech calls Abraham and asks: what did you see, that you did this thing?

teach.h: NO FEAR OF GOD IN THIS PLACE.
teach.b: And Abraham answers: "Surely the fear of God is not in this place." He assumed these people had no conscience. The story shows otherwise.
Abimelech returns Sarah, gives sheep and oxen and servants, and says: my land is before you; live wherever you like.
Then Abraham prays for Abimelech's household, and they're healed.
The story lets the founder of the Jewish people be wrong about strangers, and lets a foreign king be the one with the clean heart.

how: Jewish commentators read Genesis 20 as a story in which Abraham's fear of strangers proves mistaken, and note that here God calls Abraham a prophet who will pray for the king.

o: and he prayed, Abraham's words for the king
and he planted, Abraham's tree in Beersheba
and he appeared, how the portion opens

games.q: who did what — tap the pairs.
p: a clean heart and clean hands
came to the king in a dream

s: Abimelech knowingly took a married woman
he was told she was Abraham's sister, and God kept him from sinning.
God tells Abimelech that Abraham is a prophet
a prophet who will pray for him, God says, and Abraham does.
Abraham turned out to be right about Gerar
he feared there was no fear of God there. the king proved decent and generous.

games.q: you're Abimelech. God warns you in a dream that the woman in your house is married. what do you do?
o: hide it and hope no one finds out.
protest your innocence, return her, and give gifts.
games.why: he protests he acted with a clean heart, returns Sarah, gives gifts and offers his land. God agrees he was innocent.

practice: Bring back a time someone you had braced against, a new neighbor, an official at a counter, a coworker, a person on the street, turned out to be kind or fair. Remember what they actually did, then what you had expected instead.
Let the gap between the two sit with you for a moment, without judging yourself.

wordCard.voice: Vayera. The portion where Abraham fears a foreign king, and the king turns out more upright than he feared.

orig.note: Hebrew: a prophet; what God calls Abraham in Abimelech's dream.

carryVoice: Your line: goodness is everywhere. Even in Gerar, where Abraham had expected none. Until tomorrow.

sources.q: Surely the fear of God is not in this place
